findings.title: Persisted-index reuse fingerprints only id, kind, text/title byte length and updatedAt; changed filters, keywords, captions, OCR text or localizations keep a stale index (Service code, outside module files)
findings.spec_ref: 9.1 rule 6 (indexed context persists under its own file), 6 (persisted files), 9.1 rule 5 / 4.1 (filters are hard constraints)
locations: /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronSearchEngine/Sources/ZTronSearchEngine/Index/LexicalIndex.swift:187-207 (content check skipped when expected fingerprint is empty)
findings.summary:
fingerprint(of:) mixes in only the id, the kind, the UTF-8 length of the text and title, and updatedAt. It leaves out keywords, caption, OCR text, localized strings, filters and embeddings, and it misses text edits that keep the byte length.

When the fingerprint matches, the file is memory-mapped and projection is skipped entirely. The only place this limitation is stated is the doc comment of the internal function ('Edits that keep all of them need an explicit refresh()'). The public .files documentation does not mention it.

findings.title: SearchLimits clamps are bypassed by its public properties: prefixExpansions = 0 or lexicalCandidates <= 0 crash the indexed strategy, while the scan strategy keeps working
findings.spec_ref: 10 (bounded work limits), 9.1 rule 3 (both strategies behave identically)
findings.summary:
SearchLimits.init clamps its values with max(1, ...), but the properties are public vars, so assigning to them afterwards skips the clamp.
- With limits.prefixExpansions = 0, which is a natural way to switch prefix matching off, IndexTermSource.prefixExpansions calls selector.accepts on an empty TopSelector, and accepts reads elements[-1].
- With limits.lexicalCandidates = 0 or a negative value, prepareScratch leaves the slot array empty, and admitCandidates writes slots[0] before checking the limit.

findings.title: SearchableID == is Unicode canonical equivalence but the index identifies documents by UTF-8 bytes: remove/contains miss, 'equal' duplicates appear, scan and indexed strategies diverge, and < is inconsistent with ==
findings.spec_ref: 4 and 9.1 rule 1 (ids unique inside a context), 9.1 rule 3 (identical ranking across strategies)
findings.summary:
SearchableID's synthesized Hashable uses String equality, which treats canonically equivalent strings as equal. So the NFC and NFD spellings of 'café' are == and hash equally. Batch dedup and the scan engine therefore merge them into one id.

The index, however, hashes and compares raw UTF-8 bytes in ordinal(ofID:). Separately, < compares bytes, so for two == ids one of them is also < the other, which breaks Comparable's rules.

findings.title: Paging arithmetic overflows: SearchQuery.limit = Int.max with a cursor offset > 0 traps (ScanIndex, and the same pattern in SearchService paging and suggestions)
findings.spec_ref: 9 / 9.1 (paging, ScanIndex.hits)
findings.summary: `start + max(0, query.limit)` uses trapping arithmetic, and SearchQuery.limit is a public Int with no clamp. Int.max is the usual way to ask for 'no limit'. The suggestions code has the same problem with `limit * 4` and `limit + 1`.

findings.title: Filter-only queries on the indexed strategy keep the first 2,000 live documents in segment order, so the hits depend on upsert/merge history
findings.spec_ref: 10 (at most 2,000 candidates), 9.1 rule 3
findings.summary: A query with only filters or kinds gives every admitted document the same score of 1, so the result list is sorted by id. But it is sorted only over whichever 2,000 documents came first in segment and ordinal order. install reorders segments by live count, and merges and saves change that order.

findings.title: Plans with more than 64 clauses (bigram fallback) give later clauses match bit 0, so documents matching only those clauses are dropped
findings.summary: The parser caps clauses at 64. The planner's bigram fallback, however, adds one plan clause for every matched bigram, so a long CJK or Thai query can push the plan past 64 clauses. Clauses from index 64 onward still add to the score but contribute match bit 0, and a document whose match mask is 0 is dropped from the list. Both strategies share this code, so parity is not broken.

findings.title: A row with a literal and a localized key in the same role loses the literal from its field: it is moved to localizedAlt, even under the base language
findings.spec_ref: 9.2 rule 3 (literals keep their declared language; only other preferred languages feed localizedAlt), 9.2 rule 4 / 15.9 (row ranks like the same memory item), section 5
findings.summary: For a keyed field, the row projector writes the resolved string for every catalog language, base language included, into searchLocalizations[tag] (for .text, into localizedTexts[tag]). Literal fields of the same role go only to the base surface. So for the active language, the localization holds only the key's string. SearchProjector then treats the base surface (literal plus key string) as shadowed and demotes it to localizedAlt. That field has a BM25F weight of 0.5, against 1.0 for text and 4.0 for keywords. With the base locale and no secondary languages, localizedAlt should be empty.

findings.title: The chat idle-unload timer can fire while a new turn is retrieving or assembling its prompt, and cancels that turn
findings.spec_ref: 14.3 rules 4-5 (unload after 120 s idle), 14.4 lifecycle
findings.summary: send() neither bumps `use` nor cancels idleTask. runTurn sets the lifecycle to .generating only after three steps: retrieval (semantic and rerank phases, up to the 300 + 400 ms caps), source rendering (several countTokens calls per source) and prompt assembly. If the idle timer set by the previous turn (or by the load) expires in that window, unloadIfIdle sees an unchanged `use` and the .ready lifecycle and calls unload(). That unloads the model and cancels every session's task, including the turn that just started.

findings.title: ChatService.load is not reentrancy-safe: unload() or a memory warning during a load is undone, and prepare() during a send-triggered load loads the weights twice
findings.spec_ref: 14.3 rule 5, 14.4 (unload on memory warning; LLM unloads before the embedding model; 1.8 GB resident)
findings.summary: There are two races. (a) unload() during .loading unloads the runtime and sets .onDisk. The suspended load(from:) then resumes and settles .ready with the runtime loaded, so a memory warning that arrives during the load is lost. (b) A send that finds the lifecycle .onDisk loads the weights in ensureLoaded without setting `preparation`. A prepare() that arrives meanwhile sees preparation == nil and starts runPreparation. That overwrites the lifecycle with .onDisk and calls model.load a second time, concurrently.

findings.title: Source truncation splits on whitespace only, so unspaced scripts (Japanese, Chinese, Thai) lose the whole caption or text of a source
findings.spec_ref: 14.3 rule 1 ('[kind:id] title, caption from its localized surface, at most 80 tokens per source'); multilingual and CJK requirements (sections 2, 5)
findings.summary: PromptAssembler.truncate keeps the longest prefix of whitespace-separated words that fits the limit. A Japanese caption or text counts as a single word. So a rendered source over 80 tokens is cut to '[kind:id] <title>,' and the caption or text disappears, even though about 60 tokens of budget remain. With a long unspaced title, only the marker remains. ChatTests exercise English only.

findings.title: Citations of ids that contain ':' are never recognised and the raw marker leaks into the transcript
findings.spec_ref: 14.3 rule 3 (markers parsed incrementally, emitted as .citation when the id is in the sources; markers never reach the text)
findings.summary: After each ':' inside a pending marker, consume() checks that everything before it is a kind: isKind(String(pending.dropFirst().dropLast())...). For '[map:m:harbor]' the second colon tests 'map:m', which is not a kind, so the bracket is released as ordinary text. marker(in:), which splits on the first colon and would accept the marker, is never reached. Such ids are legal. The engine's own SearchRowIdentity.prefixed produces them (DatabaseSourceTests uses .prefixed("m:")), and the prompt tells the model to cite ids verbatim.

findings.title: Text date columns cost up to two ISO8601DateFormatter constructions per row
findings.spec_ref: 15.9 (one page of 500 rows read, resolved and projected in 40 ms; 10k-row context in 1.5 s on the reference device)
findings.summary: SearchDateParser creates a new ISO8601DateFormatter for each option set it tries, for every value. SQLite.swift stores Date as TEXT ('yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'). SQLite's CURRENT_TIMESTAMP produces 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', which costs two constructions because the fractional-seconds attempt fails first. The adapter's database target tests use REAL dates, so this path is never measured against the budget.

findings.title: The cancellation-latency test allows 10 ms plus a quarter of the whole search, instead of 10 ms after the next checkpoint
findings.spec_ref: 15.4 'Cancellation honoured within 10 ms of the next checkpoint'; 11 (checkpoint every 1,000 postings)
findings.summary: The test asserts worst < 0.010 + full / 4, where `full` is the duration of an uncancelled run. The bound therefore grows with the search: a 400 ms debug or TSan search allows 110 ms. The test would pass with about four checkpoints per search. testTheScoringLoopChecksCancellation only shows that an already-cancelled task throws, meaning one checkpoint exists; it does not check the 1,000-unit spacing. The assertion message still claims the 10 ms gate.

findings.title: Every keyed field resolves the key in every catalog language, though only the active, fallback and secondary languages are used
findings.spec_ref: 15.9 (page and context-creation budgets)
findings.summary: For each keyed field of each row, the projector calls resolver.string(forKey:...) for every language the catalog lists and stores all the results in searchLocalizations. SearchProjector then keeps only the active language, its fallback chain and the configured secondary languages. The cost grows linearly with the number of catalog languages. Section 15.9 is specified, and tested, with only 2.

findings.title: A row's literal fields lose their declared language unless every field of the row agrees on one language
findings.spec_ref: 9.2 rule 3 ('Literal fields keep their declared language tag')
findings.summary: The row item has a single searchLanguage for its base surface. It is set only when no literal is untagged and the union of literal tags and the keys' first-resolved languages has exactly one element. Two cases get nil: a literal tagged 'fr' next to a key whose catalog base is 'en', and two literals with different tags. The literal is then tokenized and normalized without its language (DocumentAnalysis passes languages.<field> to the tokenizer), and matchedLanguage is unknown.

findings.title: Public setters bypass the clamps of RerankSpec, EditorialPolicy and SearchLimits; out-of-range values exceed the spec ceilings or trap
findings.spec_ref: 7.4 / 8 (rerank top 16, at most 32; at most 3 pins)
findings.summary: The clamps (topN 1...32, blend 0...1, maximumPins 0...3, retainedHits >= 1) run only in the initializers. The properties themselves are public vars, and the README configures profiles by mutating them. Setting topN = 64 sends 64 passages to the cross-encoder. Setting maximumPins = 10 pins ten results. A negative topN or retainedHits traps in prefix(_:).

findings.title: A non-finite cross-encoder score puts NaN into the published hits and silently disables the rerank for the head
findings.spec_ref: 7.4 (blend formula), 6 (snapshot semantics)
findings.summary: rerankPhase accepts any score array of the right length, and reranked() min-max normalizes it. An +inf score becomes NaN for that document and 0 for all the others. A NaN score breaks the sort comparator and the score mapping. The snapshot then carries NaN scores and scores above the head's top score, the cross-encoder order is lost, and no degraded flag is set.

findings.title: Wiring chat through ZTronSearch creates a retain cycle; neither the search service nor the chat service is ever freed
findings.spec_ref: 9.1 rule 6 ('releasing the service frees everything'); 11 predictable cleanup / leak tests
findings.summary: The facade installs `{ await service.unload() }` as the search service's memoryWarningPredecessor, and that closure captures the ChatService strongly. ChatService in turn holds the SearchService strongly. Releasing the facade therefore leaves both services alive, along with their index, observers and change-stream subscriptions.

findings.title: A send that arrives during a model fetch waits, uncancellably, for the whole download while holding the generation lock
findings.spec_ref: 14.3 rule 4 (a new send in the same session cancels the one in flight; other sessions queue), 14.4 cancellation target
findings.summary: runTurn takes the generation lock, then ensureLoaded parks on a CheckedContinuation until the running preparation ends. Cancelling the turn (with stop, or with a new send in the same session) does not resume it. The cancelled turn holds the lock until the download finishes or is cancelled, and every other session queues behind it.

findings.title: query.limit = 0 yields a cursor that never advances
findings.spec_ref: 6 rule 8 (paging continues the final snapshot's list)
findings.summary: The page end is computed as start + max(0, limit). With limit 0, every snapshot and page is empty, but nextCursor is SearchCursor(offset: start) while documents remain. page(after:) therefore returns the same cursor forever.

findings.title: The prompt budget counts message contents only, not the chat template's per-message tokens, and the test measures the same quantity
findings.spec_ref: 14.3 rule 2 (prompt inside contextWindow - maxNewTokens - 64)
findings.summary: PromptAssembler sums countTokens(content) per message. The role headers and separators that the runtime's chat template adds are not counted; ChatML-style templates use about 4-6 tokens per message. Those tokens have to fit in the fixed 64-token margin. With a long kept history the overhead grows with the message count (about 150 tokens for 30 messages), so prompt + maxNewTokens can exceed the window. The test sums the same content-only counts.

findings.title: SearchError.missingLocalizedStringResolver is declared but never thrown; keyed fields are silently dropped when no resolver is set
findings.spec_ref: 9.2 (localizedStrings 'required when any field is a localized key')
findings.summary: The public error case documents 'A field is declared as a localization key but the context has no resolver', but nothing produces it. Instead, the projector emits a debug-only unresolvedLocalizationKey per field per row and indexes nothing for that field. A misconfigured context loads successfully with empty titles. testAContextWithoutAResolverIndexesNothingForKeyedFields enshrines the silent behaviour.

findings.title: A large `limit` crashes the HNSW search (Int.max) or pins scratch memory proportional to the limit
findings.spec_ref: 10 (bounded work), 15.2 (memory)

findings.title: The 'Not a gate' isotropic HNSW test enforces the latency gate and fails the CI quality-targets step
findings.spec_ref: 15.1 (HNSW ANN top 50: 5 ms p95, recall@10 >= 0.95), 16
findings.summary: testRecallOnIsotropicTopicsIsReportedAndRecoversWithBreadth is documented as 'Not a gate' and runs measure(..., efSearch: 256), four times the specification's breadth. measure() asserts the scaled 5 ms budget (XCTAssertLessThan(measurement.coldP95, allowed)) on every call. findings.title: Vector and graph files with tombstone bits beyond the row/node count are accepted, and rows appended later are born tombstoned
findings.spec_ref: 7.3 (memory-mapped vector and graph files); damaged or hostile file handling
findings.summary: Both decoders compare the live or deleted count with Bitset.population. That counts every bit of every word, including bits above the row/node count in the last word, and nothing requires those bits to be zero. HNSWIndex(store:graphAt:) compares tombstones only for 0..<store.count. A file with such a bit, and its count adjusted to match, is accepted with a phantom tombstone. The next appended row or node lands on that bit (upsert appends at `count`, and HNSWGraph.insert only reserves words) and is tombstoned from birth.

findings.title: Id identity differs between mapped rows (byte compare) and the in-memory overlay (canonical equivalence)
findings.spec_ref: 7.3 (vector store keyed by SearchableID)
findings.summary: SearchableID equality is String equality (canonical equivalence). ordinal(of:) looks base rows up with a byte-wise binary search, while the overlay and build's de-duplication use a Swift dictionary. An id stored in the file as NFC is not found under its NFD spelling. An upsert of the NFD spelling therefore appends a second live row for an id that compares equal. remove() of the NFC spelling then retires the appended row (found through the overlay) and leaves the base row live.

findings.title: 'Relevance gates among 100,000 distractors' adds no competition: distractors are built never to match a golden query, and the numbers are identical at 5,000 and 100,000
findings.spec_ref: 15.3; section 15 preamble (100k items)
findings.summary: The fixtures are built so that distractors never compete. Titles and keywords are pseudo-words. No pseudo-word shares its first three letters with a lexicon word. Lemmas appear only after the 24th word of a body. Synonyms and reserved translations never appear. A distractor therefore cannot take a head position through title, prefix, keyword, paraphrase, translation or embedding. Near-miss competitors are absent: shared prefixes, typo neighbours, titles that share words. The CI's 100k relevance run exercises scale only, not relevance under competition.

findings.title: The semantic, cross-language and rerank gates are reached only with oracle fakes built from the queries' own lexicon; the rerank stage changes no metric, so 'never below fused' holds by equality
findings.spec_ref: 15.3 (paraphrase recall 0.75, cross-language recall 0.70, reranked NDCG 0.85 and never below fused)
findings.summary: The fake embedding maps the lexicon's concepts (synonyms and translations) to orthonormal vectors. The fake reranker scores concept overlap. findings.title: The 'timeout-guarded' deadlock test cannot time out, because withTaskGroup waits for the hung child
findings.spec_ref: Section 11 liveness table (no deadlock: Thread Sanitizer in CI; timeout-guarded tests)
findings.summary: When the timer child returns nil, the closure calls cancelAll, but withTaskGroup still awaits all of its children. A deadlocked operation, or one with a lost continuation, never completes. withTimeout therefore never returns, and XCTAssertEqual(finished, true, '... no deadlock, no lost continuation') is never reached. Only the CI job timeout (45 or 90 minutes) ends the run.
